1: The sky was opened, and I saw a vision: an aged woman in a shining garment, holding a book, and she said to me: Hermas, who are you to accuse me? Am I not the one who brought you up? And I said: I did not accuse you, lady; I only desire to know what you mean. And she said: The book is the commandments, and the commandments are for the whole world, and you are one of the world — so take them and live.

She showed me a tower being built upon the water, built with square stones that fitted exactly, and the builder was the Church, and the stones were the saints, and the water was the faith that carries them. And some stones were rejected for being round, and I asked why, and she said: Because they would roll away from the place where they were laid.
2: First of all, believe that God is one, who created all things and set them in order, and brought all things from non-existence into being, and contains all things, and is Himself alone uncontained. Believe in Him, and fear Him, and in fearing Him be restrained; and you shall live.

Hold simplicity and be guileless, and you shall be as the children who know no evil and whose minds have no malice. Do not deliberate with yourself about anything — for deliberation is the mother of doubt, and doubt is the mother of denial.

Be patient, and you shall rule over all the wickedness of the world. Patience is greater than the walls of a city, and its walls are not of stone but of peace; and the army that besieges it cannot name it, and what cannot be named cannot be taken.
3: As a field that is fenced and tilled and watered brings forth fruit in its season, so the servant of God who keeps the commandments bears fruit that does not rot. And the fence of the field is the church, and the tilling is repentance, and the water is the word, and the fruit is the mercy you show.

I saw a great willow, spreading far and wide, and under its shade all who called upon the name of the Lord came and were sheltered. And the shepherd said: This willow is the law of God, given to the whole world; and the law is the Son of God, and the shade is His mercy, and the leaves are His commandments, and they are given to the least and the greatest alike.

The shepherd showed me twelve mountains, and on each a different kind of people: the faithful, the rich who trusted in riches, the hypocrites, the double-minded, the sorrowful, the liars — and on the last, the penitent, who wept and were welcomed. For the last mountain is open to all the others, and its gate is low so that the bowed may enter, and its name is Repentance, and it is the tallest mountain of all.
